content: Eposino is a recombinant human erythropoietin (EPO) injection designed for administration either intravenously (IV) or subcutaneously (SC). It is a product of a biotechnology collaboration between Peking University Weiming Group and Sinogen (China) Ltd. Erythropoietin is produced using recombinant DNA technology in mammalian cell cultures and is available as a therapeutic agent. Clinically, it is utilized in the treatment of anemia caused by chronic renal failure or cancer chemotherapy. Additionally, EPO is one of the most commonly used performance-enhancing drugs in endurance sports. Eposino is supplied in vials or pre-filled single-use syringes. Unlike traditional syringes, the Eposino Rediject system eliminates dead space in the chamber, preventing the loss of nearly 10% of the total dosage. Moreover, the use of a double-beveled thin needle minimizes pain at the injection site and reduces the risk of iatrogenic infection. An online distributor, .com, became the first internet-based vendor to globally offer recombinant human erythropoietin (rhEPO) for sale in the mid-2000s. The company claims to provide clients with a safe, secure, private, and reliable means to remotely purchase rhEPO, ensuring quick delivery via express courier to their chosen destination. Based in Hyderabad, India, .com also published an unauthorized English translation of the book L.A. Confidential: Lance Armstrong's Secrets.
